o1.biggest_strength: Concepts are genuinely distinct and every hook is lifted from real review or survey language, with the scratch risk handled up front and the first-three pick justified by cost per purchase.
o1.biggest_mistake: The concept 4 test budget uses a blended ₹1,515 cost while concept 3 uses ₹1,058, so the three test budgets and the 'tenth of spend' claim don't quite reconcile with the broader 396-purchase base.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the test-budget maths so each concept's spend figure and pass/stop rule trace to the same audience cost, and name the winner threshold explicitly.

o2.biggest_strength: The reading of the numbers is sharp, including the women-25-40 purchase share and a direct test of the current colour-background style, and the 'check your airline's limit' caveat is exactly the right hedge.
o2.biggest_mistake: The three concept hooks are close cousins of each other and of current ads (belt, lift, quiet), and concept 2's 'will it pass the gate check?' hook edges toward implying a guarantee the brand forbids.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Push two of the eight concepts into angles the data doesn't already suggest (a gift-occasion story, a colour-scratch honesty angle) and give each a single test variable with a stated budget.

reason: Output 1 is more disciplined: its rules block the scratch and front-pocket traps, its hooks are verbatim customer lines, and its first-three order is argued from the money rather than from general sense. Output 2 is strong but reads as a slightly safer re-cut of the same idea set.
